faq.title: FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS
faq.subtitle: Guide for Travelers and Custodians
faq.desc: Everything you need to know before embarking on your journey to the heart of the Sacred Valley.

items.question: Is prior experience with medicinal plants necessary?
items.answer: No. Our spiritual guardians evaluate each visitor and design a personalized process according to their sensitivity level and experience.

items.question: How do I get to the sanctuary from Cusco?
items.answer: Pampa Ñusta is 45 minutes from Cusco. We offer private transport from the airport, or you can take a colectivo to Pisac and we will pick you up in town.

items.question: What does the volunteering program include?
items.answer: It includes accommodation in high mountain tents or shared domes, 3 vegetarian meals a day, bioconstruction workshops, and free access to the sanctuary.

items.question: Do you have internet connection (Wi-Fi)?
items.answer: Yes. We have satellite connection in designated areas, but we encourage digital disconnection to fully immerse in nature.

items.question: Can I bring children?
items.answer: Of course! The Living School is designed specifically to integrate children into nature with alternative learning methodologies.

joinus.residencia_desc: For those who have heard the deep call to become permanent guardians of the sanctuary.
joinus.subtitle: INTEGRATION PATHS
joinus.voluntariado_desc: Immerse yourself in permaculture and bioconstruction. Ideal for travelers who want to learn while serving the earth.
joinus.retiro_desc: Deep isolation, traditional diets, and internal work guided by our Andean-Amazonian masters.
joinus.title: JOIN THE TRIBE
joinus.intro_desc: The call of the mountain is for those who feel the deep desire to reconnect with Pachamama. There are different paths to integrate into our community, from short learning visits to becoming a permanent guardian of the sanctuary.

form.name: Custodian Name
form.processing: Integrating your energy into the sanctuary...

ayni.subtitle: Ecosystem Support
ayni.title: MAKE AYNI EFFECTIVE
ayni.desc: Reciprocity (Ayni) allows the sanctuary to breathe and grow. Your contribution funds native seeds, watering hours, ecological classrooms, and the genetic maintenance of our sacred cacti.
ayni.calculator_desc: Slide to visualize how your contribution translates into concrete actions within the archaeological park.

identity.mission_desc: To protect and cultivate the genetic bank of the sacred Wachuma cactus and native seeds, providing an alternative education space for children and a comprehensive healing refuge through ceremonies and regenerative technologies.
identity.subtitle: The Heart of the Sanctuary
identity.title: Pampa Ñusta Identity
identity.who_desc: We are a collective of earth guardians located in the community of Maska, Pisac. We form a living ecovillage dedicated to preserving ancestral Andean memory, bioconstruction, and the spiritual legacy of the Andes for future generations.
identity.vision_desc: To become a global epicenter of ancestral wisdom and permaculture, where humanity remembers how to live in harmony with Pachamama, expanding collective consciousness from the Sacred Valley of the Incas to the entire world.

hero.subtitle: Ecological Sanctuary • Certified Organic • Living Permaculture

location.subtitle: SANCTUARY COORDINATES
location.desc: Strategically located at the foot of the imposing archaeological complex of Pisac. Our sanctuary is nourished by the glacial waters of the major Apus, creating a perfect microclimate for the conservation of medicine and seeds.
location.title: SACRED TERRITORY

donation_banner.subtitle: The Cycle of Reciprocity
donation_banner.desc: The preservation of the terraces, native seeds, and the legacy of Pampa Ñusta is sustained through Ayni, the ancient Andean practice of giving and receiving. If you feel the call to be part of this custody, we invite you to discover our adoption program.

leaders.subtitle: The Guardians
leaders.title: Spiritual Leaders of America
leaders.desc: Meet the wise souls who guard the vision and medicine of Pampa Ñusta. Representatives of diverse traditions uniting under the prophecy of the Eagle and the Condor.

lider1.name: Taita Inti
lider1.desc: Guardian of ancestral medicine and protector of the apus of the Sacred Valley. His lineage preserves the healing songs and deep respect for Pachamama.

lider2.name: Abuela Yaku
lider2.desc: Guardian of master plants and water wisdom, connecting the spiritual world with the earthly through the millennial heritage of the deep jungle.

lider3.name: Chief White Eagle
lider3.desc: Represents the ancient prophecy of the union of the Eagle and the Condor, bringing the teachings of unity and peace from the northern tribes.

lider4.name: Master Killa
lider4.desc: Guides souls through the expansion of consciousness in the mountains. His medicine opens the heart and restores the spiritual balance of those who visit him.

brand.desc: Protecting the ancestral memory of the Sacred Valley. An archaeological sanctuary, a botanical reserve of Wachuma, and a sustainable ecovillage vibrating in Ayni.

newsletter.title: Archaeological Logbook
newsletter.desc: Receive monthly chronicles about findings, astronomical events, and restoration progress.

wachuma.title: Trichocereus Pachanoi · 7 Ribs
wachuma.tagline: Ancestral Genetics of the Sacred Valley
wachuma.cinemaLogline: We safeguard mother cuttings dating back to ancient Incan agricultural terraces.
keyHighlights: Rescue of endemic species from the Andes threatened by urban expansion.
Natural healing with Sacred Ash to prevent fungal infections.
Reforestation of 1,000 specimens in the next 3 years.
wachuma.quote: «A cactus carries in its water the memory of a thousand rains and the wisdom of the stars.»
wachuma.projectVision: Our goal is not just to plant cacti, but to preserve a library of living DNA. The San Pedro (Wachuma) is the spiritual axis of the Andes. We rescue giant specimens that were about to be destroyed by urbanization.
objectives: Establish the largest genetic reserve of Trichocereus in the Sacred Valley.
Develop a protocol for organic propagation without synthetic chemicals.
Offer adoption certificates to global guardians.

roadmap.title: Genetic Mapping
roadmap.description: Expeditions to remote areas to locate centenary cactus grandfathers.

roadmap.title: Cutting Extraction
roadmap.description: Ritual cuts and sun healing using sacred ash.

roadmap.title: Dome Rooting
roadmap.description: Planting in sterile river sand to guarantee 100% rooting.

wachuma.neuromarketingHook: You are not funding a garden; you are saving the genetic code of the oldest ancestral medicine in the Americas. If we don't protect it today, tomorrow it will be a myth.

reina.title: The Awakening of the Queen
reina.cinemaLogline: A spectacular flower that opens its giant petals only for one night a year.
keyHighlights: Nocturnal observation of the blooming of the Queen of the Night (Epiphyllum).
Collection of pollen for manual cross-fertilization.
Extraction of the sacred sweet fruit (Pitaya Andina).
reina.quote: «The most sublime beauty reveals itself only in the absolute darkness of the night.»
reina.projectVision: The flowering of the Queen of the Night is a celestial event. We organize nocturnal vigils to manually pollinate these flowers, as their natural pollinators are endangered. It is an act of pure devotion to nature.
objectives: Ensure the reproduction of nocturnal cacti.
Document the lunar cycle and its effect on sap flow.
Harvest the medicinal fruit for communal diets.

roadmap.title: Bud Monitoring
roadmap.description: Daily photographic record of the flower bud swelling.

roadmap.title: Night Watch
roadmap.description: Guard shifts during the full moon to capture the full opening.

roadmap.title: Fruit Collection
roadmap.description: Careful extraction of the sweet fruit months later to extract its black seeds.

reina.neuromarketingHook: It only opens one night a year. Witnessing this moment requires patience, respect, and synchrony with the cosmos. Are you ready to understand the timing of nature?

semillas.title: Conservation of Native Seeds
semillas.cinemaLogline: The millennial ark of giant corns, wild potatoes, and golden grains that feed the future.
keyHighlights: Underground bioclimatic seed bank to preserve humidity and temperature.
Cultivation without agrochemicals or genetic modifications.
semillas.quote: «He who keeps a seed, holds the promise of tomorrow in his hands.»
semillas.projectVision: We are losing the biodiversity that took the Incas thousands of years to develop. This vault is a living ark. We don't just store seeds; we plant them, adapt them, and return them to the communities.
objectives: Safeguard at least 50 varieties of native seeds.
Train local farmers in biological conservation.
Create a free seed distribution network.

roadmap.title: Bioclimatic Construction
roadmap.description: Building the underground vault (Qollqa) to maintain a constant temperature.

roadmap.title: Chhalay (Exchange)
roadmap.description: Journey through high communities exchanging rare and endemic seeds.

roadmap.title: Annual Planting
roadmap.description: Mandatory planting every 3 years so the seed maintains its viability and vital vigor.

semillas.neuromarketingHook: An extinct seed never returns. Your support allows us to keep alive the most powerful food gene bank of the Incan civilization.

ninos.title: Children's Recreation Center
ninos.tagline: Free Nature School and Andean Play
ninos.cinemaLogline: Where childhood learns with hands in the mud, stories under the Queñual tree, and songs to the river.
keyHighlights: Spaces built by the children themselves using adobe and recycled wood.
Curriculum based on the agricultural calendar and lunar cycles.
Integration of local indigenous children with foreign children.
ninos.quote: «If we want to heal the earth, we must first allow the children to touch it.»
ninos.projectVision: The current educational system disconnects humans from their environment. Here, the river is the blackboard and the forest is the classroom. We educate free, conscious leaders capable of regenerating the planet.
objectives: Provide a safe and natural space for the children of the Pisac community.
Teach practical permaculture from an early age.
Revalue the Quechua language through music and play.

roadmap.title: Natural Play Zones
roadmap.description: Creation of the stone labyrinth, zip line over the river, and small adobe houses.

roadmap.title: Children's Gardens
roadmap.description: Assignment of land plots so each child is responsible for their harvest.

roadmap.title: Summer Camps
roadmap.description: Launch of 7-day immersive children's retreats without screens or technology.

ninos.neuromarketingHook: You are not investing in a traditional school; you are sponsoring the reconnection of an entire generation with the intelligence of the Earth. The future depends on the sensitivity we cultivate in their hearts today.

ceremonias.title: Master Plant Ceremonies
ceremonias.tagline: The Sacred Fire of Healing and Vision
ceremonias.cinemaLogline: Sacred circles of introspection guided by lineage healers from the Sacred Valley.
keyHighlights: Physical and spiritual preparation with a prior 7-day Andean diet.
Opening of the sacred space with an offering to Pachamama (Haywarikuy).
Nocturnal fire ceremony facing the sacred snow-capped peaks of Apu Linli.
Psychological and emotional integration circle at dawn with a flower bath.
ceremonias.quote: «To heal is not to erase the pain, but to return the soul to its original cosmic axis.»
ceremonias.projectVision: Our Ceremonial Maloka is not a tourist space; it is a hospital for the spirit. We believe in the guided, ethical, and respectful use of master plants to achieve mental and emotional detoxification of a depressed and anxious society.
objectives: Offer an absolute framework of physical and psychological safety for sacred medicine.
Strictly respect the lineages and songs of the Andean Taitas.
Facilitate post-ceremony therapeutic integration to guarantee real life changes.

roadmap.title: Circular Maloka
roadmap.description: Raising the octagonal structure with noble woods and a wild straw roof, acoustically aligned.

roadmap.title: Central Altar
roadmap.description: Design of the smokeless fire pit and consecration of the space by healers of the Q'eros nation.

roadmap.title: Temazcal (Sweat Lodge)
roadmap.description: Construction of the hot stone dome for purification prior to working with medicine.

ceremonias.neuromarketingHook: Closing your eyes around the fire here is not just another experience; it is the breaking point where your past life ends and your true essence is revealed. There are only 10 spots per full moon.

talleres.title: Immersive Workshops 4+ Days
talleres.tagline: Learning to Live from the Earth in Community
talleres.cinemaLogline: Residential immersion in Andean permaculture, bioconstruction, and regenerative living in an ecovillage.
keyHighlights: Learn to build with adobe, quincha, and sustainable bamboo.
Design of food forests and gray water management.
Vegetarian diet from farm to table harvested by yourself.
talleres.quote: «The best rebellion is to grow your own food and build your own shelter.»
talleres.projectVision: We want to empower people so they stop depending on an extractive system. In these workshops, we teach ancient techniques combined with modern science so you can design your own ecological oasis anywhere in the world.
objectives: Transfer ancestral techniques of architecture without cement.
Teach how to harvest and store rainwater.
Form a global network of active permaculturists.

roadmap.title: Eco-Student Domes
roadmap.description: Construction of ecological dormitories with dry toilets and solar showers to house apprentices.

roadmap.title: Tool Equipment
roadmap.description: Acquisition of mud mixers, carpentry tools, and a soil laboratory.

roadmap.title: University Alliances
roadmap.description: Achieve international backing to certify the Permaculture Design Course (PDC).

talleres.neuromarketingHook: It's not a course, it's a deep 'reset' to your survival skills. Learning to build a wall with your own hands changes the way you see the universe forever. Few spots remain for the next season.

intro.title: Legend of the Enchanted Ñusta
intro.subtitle: ORIGINAL DOCUMENTARY: ANCESTRAL MEMORY
intro.description: Inquill Chumpi and Prince Asto Rímac: love, a pact with the Apus, and their transmutation into stone guardians of the harvest in Pisac.

piedras.title: Feminine & Masculine Energy
piedras.subtitle: TUTELARY MONOLITHS OF PISAC
piedras.description: The Ñusta and the Prince transmuted into living rock, teaching the sacred planting (Tarpuy) to the children and the Andean people.

acto1.title: The Impossible Challenge
acto1.subtitle: ACT 01 · 0% ROCK
acto1.description: Huayllapumap Sasa Munaynin. The chieftain demanded the construction of a stone bridge or terraces in a single night to prove the prince's courage. Princess Inquill Chumpi prayed to the Apus for her beloved.

acto2.title: The Oath of Asto Rimac
acto2.subtitle: ACT 02 · 25% ROCK
acto2.description: Asto Rimacpa Tuta Ruwaynin. «Walk without hesitation toward the sacred peak; if your eyes seek my fatigue, the mountain will claim our souls.» Deep in love, the warrior summons hidden forces and the Apus to raise the pillars in the dark.

acto3.title: The Forbidden Gaze
acto3.subtitle: ACT 03 · 65% ROCK
acto3.description: Hark'asqa Qaway. Almost at dawn, with the work about to be completed, Inquill Chumpi could not resist and turned to see if her beloved was surviving the titanic effort. The pact with the mountain was broken.

acto4.title: The Eternal Petrification
acto4.subtitle: ACT 04 · 100% ROCK
acto4.description: Wiñay Rumi Tukupuy. Both were turned into granite. Today, the Female Stone guards the fertility of the water, and the Male Stone guides the heat of the sun on the terraces, blessing the Tarpuy Raymi.

ecologico.title: ECOLOGICAL IMPACT
ecologico.subtitle: REGENERATION OF THE BIOSPHERE
ecologico.description: We transformed an eroded land into a living forest. Today we safeguard more than 3,000 endemic species, purifying the air and restoring the ancestral water cycle of the Sacred Valley.

social.title: SOCIAL IMPACT
social.subtitle: EMPOWERING THE COMMUNITY
social.description: We do not hire employees, we forge guardians. The local families of Pisac are our partners, integrating their millennial wisdom with a fair economy that breaks the cycle of poverty.

educacion.title: EDUCATIONAL IMPACT
educacion.subtitle: THE LIVING SCHOOL
educacion.description: We return childhood to the earth. Through our free nature school, local and visiting children learn botany, bioconstruction, and the Quechua language away from screens.

tecnologico.title: TECHNOLOGICAL IMPACT
tecnologico.subtitle: ANCESTRAL ENGINEERING
tecnologico.description: We merge the precision of Incan hydraulic engineering with modern renewable energies. 100% solar energy, dry ecological toilets, and gray water treatment via phytodepuration.

economico.title: ECONOMIC IMPACT
economico.subtitle: CIRCULAR ECONOMY (AYNI)
economico.description: The sanctuary is a self-sustaining organism. Every donation, retreat, and volunteer program feeds a closed circuit where wealth returns to the land and its caretakers.

espiritual.title: SPIRITUAL IMPACT
espiritual.subtitle: GLOBAL AWAKENING
espiritual.description: We are an epicenter of deep emotional healing. Through the ethical and traditional use of master plants, hundreds of souls have found their cosmic purpose under our mountains.

t1.quote: Pampa Ñusta is not a retreat, it is a portal. The Wachuma ceremony under the stars completely rewired my perspective on life. I arrived looking for answers and left with an expanded heart.
t1.name: Sarah Jenkins

t2.quote: Seeing my children play in the mud, learning Quechua and respecting the earth in the Living School is the greatest gift. This ecovillage proves that another world is possible.
t2.name: Mateo Carrasco

t3.quote: The rigor and respect with which they treat the ancestral medicine is unparalleled. The Taitas guide with an ancient love. The integration process is what truly changed my reality.
t3.name: Dr. Elena Rostova

mediahub.subtitle: GLOBAL CONNECTION
mediahub.title: MULTIMEDIA CENTER
mediahub.live_desc: Join our next live broadcast from the Ceremonial Maloka in the Sacred Valley. Share with the global community, ask questions in real-time, and receive the vibration of ancestral chants.
mediahub.gallery_desc: Very soon we will enable the historical archive of photos and videos of the ecovillage. You will be able to explore every corner, ceremony, and bioconstruction progress of the Pampa Ñusta Sanctuary.

tour360.subtitle: 02 — IMMERSIVE TOUR
tour360.desc: Get to know the ecological facilities, botanical domes, and community services of the sanctuary through our referential video and virtual tour.
tour360.immersion_desc: Immerse yourself in the immensity of the Sacred Valley through this ultra-high-definition visual expedition. This cinematic tour transports you through the bioconstruction and living heritage of each of our ecological zones.
tour360.reference_badge: Referential visual illustrating the vision and atmosphere of Pampa Ñusta

wachuma_wasi.name: Geodesic Dome & Wachuma Genetic Bank
wachuma_wasi.shortDesc: Bioclimatic geodesic greenhouse with over 40 acclimated mother lineages of Trichocereus pachanoi and peruvianus.
wachuma_wasi.neuromarketingHook: More than preserving a sacred cactus, we are decoding the genome of Andean consciousness and protecting it from climate extinction.
wachuma_wasi.scope: The scope covers 12 hectares of direct conservation and the creation of the first Trichocereus genomic bank in South America.
wachuma_wasi.fullDesc: The botanical heart of Pampa Ñusta. A passive bioclimatic geodesic dome housing the largest living collection of the sacred Wachuma cactus in the Vilcanota basin. Designed to emulate the Andean ravine microclimate with volcanic mineral substrates, zenithal ventilation, and daytime thermal capture to protect mother lineages from night frosts.

arca_semillas.name: Andean Seed Ark & Living Laboratory
arca_semillas.shortDesc: Germplasm sanctuary with over 200 native varieties of sacred corn, Andean potatoes, quinoa, and kiwicha.
arca_semillas.neuromarketingHook: In a world threatened by climate change, true wealth is not gold, but the germplasm that will guarantee food for humanity.
arca_semillas.scope: Direct impact on the food sovereignty of 18 high Andean communities in the Sacred Valley, ensuring biologically pure germplasm for the next 3 generations.
arca_semillas.fullDesc: Built as a bioclimatic vault of adobe and cured clay, the Seed Ark guards the genetic heritage of the Andes. It preserves ancestral varieties of polychrome corn, native high-altitude tubers, and sacred grains, stored in clay vessels sealed with natural beeswax that prevent pests without a single gram of agrochemicals.

escuela_viva.name: Living School & Children's Bio-Park
escuela_viva.shortDesc: Outdoor educational village with a mud amphitheater, bio-games, and Andean fauna rescue.
escuela_viva.neuromarketingHook: We do not inherit the earth from our ancestors, we borrow it from our children. Here we train the ecological leaders of tomorrow.
escuela_viva.scope: Free bilingual ecological training and emotional support for 150 boys and girls annually from vulnerable rural schools.
escuela_viva.fullDesc: An educational pilot project that merges the forest school methodology with the Andean worldview. Designed for early childhood in rural communities to revalue their original culture through bioconstruction, agriculture, and art in Quechua.

maloka_ceremonial.name: Ceremonial Maloka & Sound Space
maloka_ceremonial.shortDesc: Circular temple of bioconstruction and 432 Hz acoustics for research of master plants.
maloka_ceremonial.neuromarketingHook: Where modern psychiatry meets its limits, ancient Andean medicine opens the doors to deep healing of trauma.
maloka_ceremonial.scope: Creation of an internationally replicable clinical-traditional standard for the treatment of trauma through rigorous Andean protocols.
maloka_ceremonial.fullDesc: The Maloka is an avant-garde center where modern science and traditional medicine converge. We investigate the neuroplastic benefits of expanded states of consciousness facilitated by Andean entheogens, under an ethical, safe framework guided by ancestral lineages.

terrazas_permacultura.name: Regenerative Terraces & Solar Hydrology
terrazas_permacultura.shortDesc: Restoration of Inca terraces with photovoltaic irrigation technology and syntropic agriculture.
terrazas_permacultura.neuromarketingHook: We revive the genius of Inca engineering and empower it with 21st century solar technology to feed the future of the Andes.
terrazas_permacultura.scope: Complete restoration of 5 levels of Inca terracing and creation of the highest altitude negative carbon footprint hydro-solar model in Peru.
terrazas_permacultura.fullDesc: An agricultural innovation project that challenges the Andean drought. We have recovered abandoned pre-Hispanic terraces by integrating contemporary solar pumping and micro-sprinkler technology. The goal is to create a replicable model of food security for the high Peruvian mountains.
